title: Workload Prognosticator — continuous batching recommender with guarded-apply orchestration
creator: Aisha Kapoor
description:
Goal: Build a predictive batching recommender (Workload Prognosticator) that generates continuous batching parameter proposals (microbatch sizes, coalescing window, KV caching policy) per workload cohort and can apply them safely via a guarded-apply orchestration. Deliver measurable unit-economics improvements (target: >=6% token-cost reduction on sampled production traffic) while preserving latency SLOs (P50/P95 floor) and model-quality signals.

Scope:
- Offline workload profiler that ingests request traces (sequence lengths, KV cache flows, arrival inter-arrival times, client route tags, priority tier) and produces per-cohort feature sets.
- Scoring model: lightweight ML regressor + rule-based heuristics to recommend batch/coalesce/window params with confidence intervals.
- Guarded apply pipeline: shadow evaluation, canary cohorts, metric gating (latency, error rate, tail latency, KV hit rate, user-facing quality checks), automated rollback triggers, and manual override.
- Continuous operation: periodic re-profiling, online feedback loop from production telemetry, safe gradual rollouts, and per-recommendation audit logs.

Success metrics:
- Cost reduction: >=6% token compute cost decrease on targeted cohorts in alpha, >=3% platform-wide after 3 months of gradual rollouts.
- Latency: no more than +2% increase in P95 for canaried cohorts; no P99 regressions beyond alert thresholds.
- Reliability: automated rollback occurs for regressions and has <1% false-positive rate in alpha.
- Observability: every applied change linked to dashboard + changelog entry and diffable config history.

Approach/design notes:
- Profiling: run lightweight samplers at edge and runtime level for 24–72h windows to capture burstiness, session lengths, and KV cache hit/miss sequences. Avoid full trace export to reduce ingestion cost; use sketching (reservoir sampling + histograms) for sequence-length distribution.
- Features: sequence_length_percentiles, kv_cache_prefix_hit_rate, interarrival_10ms/50ms/90ms quantiles, request_priority, route_cardinality, avg_prompt_tokens_per_session, model_variant.
- Scoring: hybrid approach — a calibrated regressor (XGBoost or small neural net) for expected cost/latency trade-off and a safety-first rule-engine to clamp recommendations (e.g., never push microbatch above X for latency-sensitive cohorts). Maintain a confidence score and suggested rollback throttle.
- Guarded apply: pipeline stages: (1) recommend -> (2) shadow simulate (replay sampled requests to scoring engine and local runtime simulator) -> (3) canary apply to 0.5–2% of traffic (cohort-aware) -> (4) monitor gating metrics for N minutes -> (5a) promote -> (5b) rollback if gating failed. Rollout runner integrates with existing rollout APIs; require ability to pin model variant and fallback routing.

Trade-offs & risks:
- Aggressive batching reduces cost but may increase tail latency for some session patterns; balancing needs tight telemetry and a conservative initial threshold.
- Profiling and replay create additional telemetry and compute overhead; needs quota budgeting.
- False positives in rollback detection; mitigate by multi-metric composite gating and require sustained regression for T seconds before rollback.

Instrumentation & observability needs (dependencies):
- New telemetry: per-request KV-cache prefix metadata, microburst indicators, session-id join keys, and recommended-profile metadata.
- Dashboards: per-cohort cost delta, latency distributions, rollback events, confidence over time. Link to draft design doc: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/BATCH/Workload+Prognosticator+Design (placeholder).

Implementation plan (milestones):
- M1 (Week 1–2): Profiling job prototype, sample sketches from prod stencil (read-only sampling).
- M2 (Week 2–3): Scoring service v0 (regressor + rules), offline evaluation harness against historical traces.
- M3 (Week 3–4): Shadow simulator + cost/latency estimator, verify recommendations on replay.
- M4 (Week 4–5): Guarded apply orchestration, canary runner integration, metrics gating and rollback policies.
- M5 (Week 6): Alpha rollout to internal customers / low-risk cohorts; measure cost/latency.

Acceptance criteria:
- Offline evaluator: recommended configs show consistent cost saves on withheld traces with no latency regression in simulation.
- Guarded apply: can perform shadow -> canary -> promote/rollback with audit trail and automatic rollback triggers.
- Documentation: runbook, playbook describing rollback thresholds and manual escalation.
